subject.title: [Feature]: Add portable Agent Bundles for export/import across OpenClaw instances

question: Should portable Agent Bundles be a first-party core import/export contract, a backup/restore extension, or a plugin/bundle API capability?
rationale: The request spans stable CLI and Gateway surfaces plus config, workspace, skills, bindings, credentials, and runtime-state boundaries, so automation cannot choose the permanent product/security contract safely.

options.title: Design a core bundle contract
options.body: Define a first-party manifest, dry-run importer, allowlist, and security policy before accepting implementation work.

options.title: Fold into backup/restore
options.body: Treat this as an agent-scoped archive workflow and coordinate it with per-agent backup/restore/clone semantics.

options.title: Route through plugin bundles
options.body: Extend plugin or ClawHub bundle APIs only if they can express the capability without new core import/export policy.

recommendation.title: Design a core bundle contract
recommendation.body: Define a first-party manifest, dry-run importer, allowlist, and security policy before accepting implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merger of agent-area work with adjacent CLI/workspace history, making this the best available routing owner for the product boundary decision.
